lines.text: From Colombo the Swami travels north, to Jaffna, the chief centre of Hinduism in Ceylon.
lines.ph: fɹʌm kəlˈɑːmboʊ ðə swˈɑːmi tɹˈævəlz nˈɔːɹθ, tˈuː dʒˈɑːfnə, ðə tʃˈiːf sˈɛntɚɹ ʌv hˈɪnduːˌɪzəm ɪn seɪlˈɑːn.

lines.text: The Hindus of Jaffna greet him with an address of welcome.
lines.ph: ðə hˈɪnduːz ʌv dʒˈɑːfnə ɡɹˈiːt hˌɪm wɪð ɐn ɐdɹˈɛs ʌv wˈɛlkʌm.

lines.text: Their ancestors had come from South India more than two thousand years before, and brought their religion with them.
lines.ph: ðɛɹ ˈænsɛstɚz hæd kˈʌm fɹʌm sˈaʊθ ˈɪndiə mˈoːɹ ðɐn tˈuː θˈaʊzənd jˈɪɹz bᵻfˈoːɹ, ænd bɹˈɔːt ðɛɹ ɹᵻlˈɪdʒən wɪð ðˌɛm.

lines.text: Under the Portuguese and the Dutch, public worship was forbidden, and temples, two far-famed shrines among them, were razed to the ground.
lines.ph: ˌʌndɚ ðə pˌoːɹtʃəɡˈiːz ænd ðə dˈʌtʃ, pˈʌblɪk wˈɜːʃɪp wʌz fɚbˈɪdən, ænd tˈɛmpəlz, tˈuː fˈɑːɹfˈeɪmd ʃɹˈaɪnz ɐmˈʌŋ ðˌɛm, wɜː ɹˈeɪzd tə ðə ɡɹˈaʊnd.

lines.text: Yet their forefathers clung to the old faith, and now the sacred buildings are being restored.
lines.ph: jˈɛt ðɛɹ fˈɔːɹfɑːðɚz klˈʌŋ tə ðɪ ˈoʊld fˈeɪθ, ænd nˈaʊ ðə sˈeɪkɹɪd bˈɪldɪŋz ɑːɹ bˌiːɪŋ ɹᵻstˈoːɹd.

lines.text: There are more things in the Philosophy of the Hindus than are dreamt of in the Philosophy of the West.
lines.ph: ðɛɹˌɑːɹ mˈoːɹ θˈɪŋz ɪnðə fɪlˈɑːsəfi ʌvðə hˈɪnduːz ðɐn ɑːɹ dɹˈɛmpt ʌv ɪnðə fɪlˈɑːsəfi ʌvðə wˈɛst.

lines.text: The next evening, he lectures on Vedantism.
lines.ph: ðə nˈɛkst ˈiːvnɪŋ, hiː lˈɛktʃɚz ˈɔn veɪdˈɑːntɪzəm.

lines.text: The subject is very large and the time is short, he begins, so he will give only the salient points.
lines.ph: ðə sˈʌbdʒɛkt ɪz vˈɛɹi lˈɑːɹdʒ ænd ðə tˈaɪm ɪz ʃˈɔːɹt, hiː bɪɡˈɪnz, sˌoʊ hiː wɪl ɡˈɪv ˈoʊnli ðə sˈeɪliənt pˈɔɪnts.

lines.text: The word Hindu once meant simply the people who lived on the other side of the river Indus, in Sanskrit, the Sindhu.
lines.ph: ðə wˈɜːd hˈɪnduː wˈʌns mˈɛnt sˈɪmpli ðə pˈiːpəl hˌuː lˈɪvd ɔnðɪ ˈʌðɚ sˈaɪd ʌvðə ɹˈɪvɚɹ ɪndˈʌs, ɪn sˈænskɹɪt, ðˈə sˈɪndʰuː.

lines.text: The ancient Persians turned Sindhu into Hindu, and during Mohammedan rule the people took up the word themselves.
lines.ph: ðɪ ˈeɪntʃənt pˈɜːʒənz tˈɜːnd sˈɪndʰuː ˌɪntʊ hˈɪnduː, ænd dˈʊɹɹɪŋ moʊhˈæmɪdən ɹˈuːl ðə pˈiːpəl tˈʊk ˌʌp ðə wˈɜːd ðɛmsˈɛlvz.

lines.text: Today it covers Mohammedans, Christians, Jains, everyone who lives in India. It has lost its meaning.
lines.ph: tədˈeɪ ɪt kˈʌvɚz moʊhˈæmɪdənz, kɹˈɪstʃənz, dʒˈeɪnz, ˈɛvɹɪwˌʌn hˌuː lˈɪvz ɪn ˈɪndiə. ɪt hɐz lˈɔst ɪts mˈiːnɪŋ.

lines.text: Better to say Vaidikas, followers of the Vedas; or better still, Vedantists, followers of the Vedanta.
lines.ph: bˈɛɾɚ tə sˈeɪ vˈaɪdɪkəz, fˈɑːloʊɚz ʌvðə vˈeɪdəz; ɔːɹ bˈɛɾɚ stˈɪl, veɪdˈɑːntɪsts, fˈɑːloʊɚz ʌvðə veɪdˈɑːntə.

lines.text: Western scholars agree that the Vedas are the oldest of the world's sacred books.
lines.ph: wˈɛstɚn skˈɑːlɚz ɐɡɹˈiː ðætðə vˈeɪdəz ɑːɹ ðɪ ˈoʊldɪst ʌvðə wˈɜːldz sˈeɪkɹɪd bˈʊks.

lines.text: But the Vedas are not the utterance of persons. Their date has never been fixed, and never can be.
lines.ph: bˈʌt ðə vˈeɪdəz ɑːɹ nˌɑːt ðɪ ˈʌɾɚɹəns ʌv pˈɜːsənz. ðɛɹ dˈeɪt hɐz nˈɛvɚ bˌɪn fˈɪkst, ænd nˈɛvɚ kæn bˈiː.

lines.text: Other religions claim authority from a Personal God, or from angels and messengers, speaking to certain persons.
lines.ph: ˈʌðɚ ɹᵻlˈɪdʒənz klˈeɪm ɐθˈɔːɹɪɾi fɹʌm ɐ pˈɜːsənəl ɡˈɑːd, ɔːɹ fɹʌm ˈeɪndʒəlz ænd mˈɛsɪndʒɚz, spˈiːkɪŋ tə sˈɜːʔn̩ pˈɜːsənz.

lines.text: Here the claim is that the Vedas are themselves the authority: the knowledge of God, without beginning and without end. Veda comes from vid, to know.
lines.ph: hˈɪɹ ðə klˈeɪm ɪz ðætðə vˈeɪdəz ɑːɹ ðɛmsˈɛlvz ðɪ ɐθˈɔːɹɪɾi: ðə nˈɑːlɪdʒ ʌv ɡˈɑːd, wɪðˌaʊt bɪɡˈɪnɪŋ ænd wɪðˌaʊt ˈɛnd. vˈeɪdə kˈʌmz fɹʌm vˈɪd, tə nˈoʊ.

lines.text: That knowledge was discovered by the Rishis. A Rishi is a Mantra-drashta, a seer of thought that already existed.
lines.ph: ðæt nˈɑːlɪdʒ wʌz dɪskˈʌvɚd baɪ ðə ɹˈɪʃiz. ˈeɪ ɹˈɪʃi ɪz ɐ mˈæntɹədɹˈæʃtə, ɐ sˈiːɚɹ ʌv θˈɔːt ðæt ɔːlɹˌɛdi ɛɡzˈɪstᵻd.

lines.text: The Rishis were spiritual discoverers.
lines.ph: ðˈə ɹˈɪʃiz wɜː spˈɪɹɪtʃˌuːəl dɪskˈʌvɚɹɚz.

lines.text: The Vedas have two parts: the Karma Kanda, the work portion, and the Jnana Kanda, the knowledge portion.
lines.ph: ðˈə vˈeɪdəz hæv tˈuː pˈɑːɹts: ðˈə kˈɑːɹmə kˈɑːndə, ðə wˈɜːk pˈoːɹʃən, ænd ðˈə ɡjˈɑːnə kˈɑːndə, ðə nˈɑːlɪdʒ pˈoːɹʃən.

lines.text: The work portion holds the sacrifices, and the duties of the student, the householder and the recluse.
lines.ph: ðə wˈɜːk pˈoːɹʃən hˈoʊldz ðə sˈækɹᵻfˌaɪsᵻz, ænd ðə dˈuːɾiz ʌvðə stˈuːdənt, ðə hˈaʊshoʊldɚ ænd ðə ɹˈɛkluːs.

lines.text: The knowledge portion is the Vedanta, the end of the Vedas, their gist and goal: the Upanishads.
lines.ph: ðə nˈɑːlɪdʒ pˈoːɹʃən ɪz ðə veɪdˈɑːntə, ðɪ ˈɛnd ʌvðə vˈeɪdəz, ðɛɹ dʒˈɪst ænd ɡˈoʊl: ðˈə uːpˈʌnɪʃədz.

lines.text: Dualists, qualified monists, monists; Shaivites, Vaishnavites, Shaktas, Sauras, Ganapatyas: every sect must acknowledge the Upanishads.
lines.ph: dˈuːəlˌɪsts, kwˈɔlᵻfˌaɪd mˈɑːnɪsts, mˈɑːnɪsts; ʃˈaɪvaɪts, vˈaɪʃnəvaɪts, ʃˈɑːktəz, sˈaʊɹəz, ɡˌʌnəpˈɑːtjəz: ˈɛvɹi sˈɛkt mˈʌst ɐknˈɑːlɪdʒ ðə uːpˈʌnɪʃədz.

lines.text: Even the symbols of household worship, studied closely, turn out to be great ideas of the Upanishads, become part of everyday life.
lines.ph: ˈiːvən ðə sˈɪmbəlz ʌv hˈaʊshoʊld wˈɜːʃɪp, stˈʌdid klˈoʊsli, tˈɜːn ˈaʊt təbi ɡɹˈeɪt aɪdˈiəz ʌvðə uːpˈʌnɪʃədz, bɪkˌʌm pˈɑːɹt ʌv ˈɛvɹɪdˌeɪ lˈaɪf.

lines.text: Next come the Smritis, books written by particular sages. Their authority is lower.
lines.ph: nˈɛkst kˈʌm ðə smɹˈɪtiz, bˈʊks ɹˈɪʔn̩ baɪ pɚtˈɪkjʊlɚ sˈeɪdʒᵻz. ðɛɹ ɐθˈɔːɹɪɾi ɪz lˈoʊɚ.

lines.text: If a Smriti contradicts the Vedanta, the Smriti is rejected.
lines.ph: ɪf ˈeɪ smɹˈɪti kˌɑːntɹədˈɪkts ðə veɪdˈɑːntə, ðˈə smɹˈɪti ɪz ɹᵻdʒˈɛktᵻd.

lines.text: The Smritis regulate manners and customs, so they change: one for the Satya Yuga, others for the Treta, the Dwapara, the Kali Yuga.
lines.ph: ðˈə smɹˈɪtiz ɹˈɛɡjʊlˌeɪt mˈænɚz ænd kˈʌstəmz, sˌoʊ ðeɪ tʃˈeɪndʒ: wˈʌn fɚðə sˈʌtjə jˈʊɡə, ˈʌðɚz fɚðə tɹˈeɪtɑː, ðˈə dwˈɑːpəɹə, ðˈə kˈʌli jˈʊɡə.

lines.text: The principles of the Vedanta never change, because they rest on the eternal principles in man and nature.
lines.ph: ðə pɹˈɪnsɪpəlz ʌvðə veɪdˈɑːntə nˈɛvɚ tʃˈeɪndʒ, bɪkˈʌz ðeɪ ɹˈɛst ɔnðɪ ɪtˈɜːnəl pɹˈɪnsɪpəlz ɪn mˈæn ænd nˈeɪtʃɚ.

lines.text: Then the Puranas, written in the language of the people, teach philosophy through the lives of saints, kings and great men.
lines.ph: ðˈɛn ðə pʊɹˈɑːnəz, ɹˈɪʔn̩ ɪnðə lˈæŋɡwɪdʒ ʌvðə pˈiːpəl, tˈiːtʃ fɪlˈɑːsəfi θɹuː ðə lˈaɪvz ʌv sˈeɪnts, kˈɪŋz ænd ɡɹˈeɪt mˈɛn.

lines.text: And the Tantras, which in places try to revive the old sacrifices.
lines.ph: ænd ðˈə tˈʌntɹəz, wˌɪtʃ ɪn plˈeɪsᵻz tɹˈaɪ tə ɹᵻvˈaɪv ðɪ ˈoʊld sˈækɹᵻfˌaɪsᵻz.

lines.text: The first common ground: nature, Prakriti, Maya, is without beginning.
lines.ph: ðə fˈɜːst kˈɑːmən ɡɹˈaʊnd: nˈeɪtʃɚ, pɹˈʌkɹɪti, mˈɑːjɑː, ɪz wɪðˌaʊt bɪɡˈɪnɪŋ.

lines.text: God is eternally creating, never at rest. In the Gita, Krishna says that if he rested for one moment, this universe would be destroyed.
lines.ph: ɡˈɑːd ɪz ɪtˈɜːnəli kɹiːˈeɪɾɪŋ, nˈɛvɚɹ æt ɹˈɛst. ɪnðˈə ɡˈiːtɑː, kɹˈɪʃnə sˈɛz ðæt ɪf hiː ɹˈɛstᵻd fɔːɹ wˈʌn mˈoʊmənt, ðɪs jˈuːnɪvˌɜːs wʊd biː dᵻstɹˈɔɪd.

lines.text: The right word is not creation but projection. Creation suggests something coming out of nothing.
lines.ph: ðə ɹˈaɪt wˈɜːd ɪz nˌɑːt kɹiːˈeɪʃən bˌʌt pɹədʒˈɛkʃən. kɹiːˈeɪʃən sədʒˈɛsts sˈʌmθɪŋ kˈʌmɪŋ ˌaʊɾəv nˈʌθɪŋ.

lines.text: Nature grows finer and subsides, rests, and is projected forward again, with a wave-like motion throughout eternity: the law of cycles, and Pralaya.
lines.ph: nˈeɪtʃɚ ɡɹˈoʊz fˈaɪnɚ ænd sʌbsˈaɪdz, ɹˈɛsts, ænd ɪz pɹədʒˈɛktᵻd fˈɔːɹwɚd ɐɡˈɛn, wɪð ɐ wˈeɪvlˈaɪk mˈoʊʃən θɹuːˈaʊt ɪtˈɜːnᵻɾi: ðə lˈɔː ʌv sˈaɪkəlz, ˈænd pɹˈʌləjə.

lines.text: In seventeen eighty-nine, the chemist Antoine Lavoisier set down the conservation of mass: in a sealed vessel matter changes its form, but nothing is created and nothing is lost.
lines.ph: ɪn sˈɛvəntˌiːn ˈeɪtinˈaɪn, ðə kˈɛmɪst ɑːntwˈɑːn ləvwˈɑːzieɪ sˈɛt dˌaʊn ðə kˌɑːnsɚvˈeɪʃən ʌv mˈæs: ɪn ɐ sˈiːld vˈɛsəl mˈæɾɚ tʃˈeɪndʒᵻz ɪts fˈɔːɹm, bˌʌt nˈʌθɪŋ ɪz kɹiːˈeɪɾᵻd ænd nˈʌθɪŋ ɪz lˈɔst.

lines.text: So wherever the scriptures speak of a beginning and an end, they mean the beginning and the end of one cycle.
lines.ph: sˌoʊ wɛɹˈɛvɚ ðə skɹˈɪptʃɚz spˈiːk əvə bɪɡˈɪnɪŋ ænd ɐn ˈɛnd, ðeɪ mˈiːn ðə bɪɡˈɪnɪŋ ænd ðɪ ˈɛnd ʌv wˈʌn sˈaɪkəl.

lines.text: What projects the universe? Brahman: eternal, pure, awake, almighty, all-knowing, formless and partless.
lines.ph: wˌʌt pɹˈɑːdʒɛkts ðə jˈuːnɪvˌɜːs? bɹˈʌhmən: ɪtˈɜːnəl, pjˈʊɹ, ɐwˈeɪk, ɔlmˈaɪɾi, ˈɔːlnˈoʊɪŋ, fˈɔːɹmləs ænd pˈɑːɹtləs.

lines.text: But the world is unequal and cruel. One is born happy, another unhappy; one animal tears another to pieces.
lines.ph: bˌʌt ðə wˈɜːld ɪz ʌnˈiːkwəl ænd kɹˈuːəl. wˈʌn ɪz bˈɔːɹn hˈæpi, ɐnˈʌðɚɹ ʌnhˈæpi; wˈʌn ˈænɪməl tˈɪɹz ɐnˈʌðɚ tə pˈiːsᵻz.

lines.text: If God made it so, God would be worse than any devil man ever imagined.
lines.ph: ɪf ɡˈɑːd mˌeɪd ɪt sˈoʊ, ɡˈɑːd wʊd biː wˈɜːs ðɐn ˌɛni dˈɛvəl mˈæn ˈɛvɚɹ ɪmˈædʒɪnd.

lines.text: The Vedanta answers: we make it so.
lines.ph: ðˈə veɪdˈɑːntə ˈænsɚz: wiː mˌeɪk ɪt sˈoʊ.

lines.text: There is a cloud shedding its rain on all fields alike.
lines.ph: ðɛɹ ɪz ɐ klˈaʊd ʃˈɛdɪŋ ɪts ɹˈeɪn ˌɔn ˈɔːl fˈiːldz ɐlˈaɪk.

lines.text: Only the field that is well tilled gets the good of the shower. It is not the fault of the cloud.
lines.ph: ˈoʊnli ðə fˈiːld ðæt ɪz wˈɛl tˈɪld ɡˈɛts ðə ɡˈʊd ʌvðə ʃˈaʊɚ. ɪɾ ɪz nˌɑːt ðə fˈɔlt ʌvðə klˈaʊd.

lines.text: The second common ground, shared with Buddhists and Jains: life is eternal. Whatever begins in time must end in time.
lines.ph: ðə sˈɛkənd kˈɑːmən ɡɹˈaʊnd, ʃˈɛɹd wɪð bˈuːdɪsts ænd dʒˈeɪnz: lˈaɪf ɪz ɪtˈɜːnəl. wʌtˈɛvɚ bɪɡˈɪnz ɪn tˈaɪm mˈʌst ˈɛnd ɪn tˈaɪm.

lines.text: The child comes into the world with the burden of an infinite past, to work out its own past deeds.
lines.ph: ðə tʃˈaɪld kˈʌmz ˌɪntʊ ðə wˈɜːld wɪððə bˈɜːdən əvən ˈɪnfɪnət pˈæst, tə wˈɜːk ˈaʊt ɪts ˈoʊn pˈæst dˈiːdz.

lines.text: This is the law of Karma: each one of us is the maker of his own fate.
lines.ph: ðɪs ɪz ðə lˈɔː ʌv kˈɑːɹmə: ˈiːtʃ wˈʌn ʌv ˌʌs ɪz ðə mˈeɪkɚɹ ʌv hɪz ˈoʊn fˈeɪt.

lines.text: We, we, and none else, are responsible for what we suffer.
lines.ph: wˈiː, wˈiː, ænd nˈʌn ˈɛls, ɑːɹ ɹᵻspˈɑːnsᵻbəl fɔːɹ wʌt wiː sˈʌfɚ.

lines.text: If I am unhappy, it is of my own making; and that very thing shows that I can be happy if I will.
lines.ph: ɪf aɪɐm ʌnhˈæpi, ɪɾ ɪz ʌv maɪ ˈoʊn mˈeɪkɪŋ; ænd ðæt vˈɛɹi θˈɪŋ ʃˈoʊz ðæt aɪ kæn biː hˈæpi ɪf aɪ wˈɪl.

lines.text: Before the infinite will of man, even the powers of nature must bow down.
lines.ph: bᵻfˌoːɹ ðɪ ˈɪnfɪnət wɪl ʌv mˈæn, ˈiːvən ðə pˈaʊɚz ʌv nˈeɪtʃɚ mˈʌst bˌaʊ dˈaʊn.

lines.text: We cannot understand God without understanding the soul, and the way lies inward, not through external nature.
lines.ph: wiː kænˈɑːt ˌʌndɚstˈænd ɡˈɑːd wɪðˌaʊt ˌʌndɚstˈændɪŋ ðə sˈoʊl, ænd ðə wˈeɪ lˈaɪz ˈɪnwɚd, nˌɑːt θɹuː ɛkstˈɜːnəl nˈeɪtʃɚ.

lines.text: In every man and every animal, however weak or wicked, the same soul resides. The difference is only in manifestation.
lines.ph: ɪn ˈɛvɹi mˈæn ænd ˈɛvɹi ˈænɪməl, haʊˈɛvɚ wˈiːk ɔːɹ wˈɪkᵻd, ðə sˈeɪm sˈoʊl ɹᵻsˈaɪdz. ðə dˈɪfɹəns ɪz ˈoʊnli ɪn mˌænɪfɪstˈeɪʃən.

lines.text: So in India the brotherhood of man becomes the brotherhood of all life, down to the little ants.
lines.ph: sˌoʊ ɪn ˈɪndiə ðə bɹˈʌðɚhˌʊd ʌv mˈæn bɪkˌʌmz ðə bɹˈʌðɚhˌʊd ʌv ˈɔːl lˈaɪf, dˌaʊn tə ðə lˈɪɾəl ˈænts.

lines.text: Thus the sage, knowing that the same Lord inhabits all bodies, will worship every body as such.
lines.ph: ðˈʌs ðə sˈeɪdʒ, nˈoʊɪŋ ðætðə sˈeɪm lˈɔːɹd ɪnhˈæbɪts ˈɔːl bˈɑːdiz, wɪl wˈɜːʃɪp ˈɛvɹi bˈɑːdi æz sˈʌtʃ.

lines.text: The mind, Manas, is not the Atman. There is the body; then the mind, the fine body, the Sukshma Sharira; and behind the mind, the Atman, the Self.
lines.ph: ðə mˈaɪnd, mˈʌnəs, ɪz nˈɑːt ðə ˈɑːtmən. ðɛɹ ɪz ðə bˈɑːdi; ðˈɛn ðə mˈaɪnd, ðə fˈaɪn bˈɑːdi, ðˈə sˈʊkʃmə ʃəɹˈiːɹə; ænd bᵻhˌaɪnd ðə mˈaɪnd, ðˈə ˈɑːtmən, ðə sˈɛlf.

lines.text: The Atman goes from birth to death with the mind, until it manifests itself to perfection, and is free.
lines.ph: ðˈə ˈɑːtmən ɡoʊz fɹʌm bˈɜːθ tə dˈɛθ wɪððə mˈaɪnd, ʌntˈɪl ɪt mˈænɪfˌɛsts ɪtsˈɛlf tə pɚfˈɛkʃən, ænd ɪz fɹˈiː.

lines.text: There are heavens and hells too, but they are not eternal. A heaven is only this world on a bigger scale.
lines.ph: ðɛɹˌɑːɹ hˈɛvənz ænd hˈɛlz tˈuː, bˌʌt ðeɪ ɑːɹ nˌɑːt ɪtˈɜːnəl. ɐ hˈɛvən ɪz ˈoʊnli ðɪs wˈɜːld ˌɔn ɐ bˈɪɡɚ skˈeɪl.

lines.text: Those who do good for the sake of reward become gods for a time, like Indra. Indra is a position, not a person; there will be thousands of Indras.
lines.ph: ðoʊz hˌuː dˈuː ɡˈʊd fɚðə sˈeɪk ʌv ɹᵻwˈɔːɹd bɪkˌʌm ɡˈɑːdz fɚɹə tˈaɪm, lˈaɪk ˈɪndɹə. ˈɪndɹə ɪz ɐ pəzˈɪʃən, nˌɑːɾə pˈɜːsən; ðɛɹ wɪl biː θˈaʊzəndz ʌv ˈɪndɹəz.

lines.text: King Nahusha, when he died, became Indra; and when his good Karma was spent, he fell, and was born a man again.
lines.ph: kˈɪŋ nəhˈuːʃə, wˌɛn hiː dˈaɪd, bɪkˈeɪm ˈɪndɹə; ænd wɛn hɪz ɡˈʊd kˈɑːɹmə wʌz spˈɛnt, hiː fˈɛl, ænd wʌz bˈɔːɹn ɐ mˈæn ɐɡˈɛn.

lines.text: This earth is the Karma Bhumi, the land of work, from which liberation is reached.
lines.ph: ðɪs ˈɜːθ ɪz ðə kˈɑːɹmə bʰˈuːmi, ðə lˈænd ʌv wˈɜːk, fɹʌm wˈɪtʃ lˌɪbɚɹˈeɪʃən ɪz ɹˈiːtʃt.

lines.text: What is worth having? Mukti, freedom. Even a king for twenty thousand years is a slave, while time and space work on him.
lines.ph: wˌʌt ɪz wˈɜːθ hˈævɪŋ? mˈʊkti, fɹˈiːdəm. ˈiːvən ɐ kˈɪŋ fɔːɹ twˈɛnti θˈaʊzənd jˈɪɹz ɪz ɐ slˈeɪv, wˌaɪl tˈaɪm ænd spˈeɪs wˈɜːk ˈɔn hˌɪm.

lines.text: Ignorance binds. Knowledge sets the soul free, and it comes through love: love of God, and of all beings as His temples.
lines.ph: ˈɪɡnɚɹəns bˈaɪndz. nˈɑːlɪdʒ sˈɛts ðə sˈoʊl fɹˈiː, ænd ɪt kˈʌmz θɹuː lˈʌv: lˈʌv ʌv ɡˈɑːd, ænd ʌv ˈɔːl bˈiːɪŋz æz hɪz tˈɛmpəlz.

lines.text: There are two ideas of God in the scriptures.
lines.ph: ðɛɹˌɑːɹ tˈuː aɪdˈiəz ʌv ɡˈɑːd ɪnðə skɹˈɪptʃɚz.

lines.text: The Personal God: creator, preserver and destroyer, the eternal Father and Mother of the universe, eternally separate from us.
lines.ph: ðə pˈɜːsənəl ɡˈɑːd: kɹiːˈeɪɾɚ, pɹɪzˈɜːvɚɹ ænd dᵻstɹˈɔɪɚ, ðɪ ɪtˈɜːnəl fˈɑːðɚ ænd mˈʌðɚɹ ʌvðə jˈuːnɪvˌɜːs, ɪtˈɜːnəli sˈɛpɹət fɹʌm ˌʌs.

lines.text: And the Impersonal: not He, but It. Not knowing, not thinking, not creating, for these belong to want and bondage.
lines.ph: ænd ðɪ ɪmpˈɜːsənəl: nˈɑːt hiː, bˈʌt ɪt. nˌɑːt nˈoʊɪŋ, nˌɑːt θˈɪŋkɪŋ, nˌɑːt kɹiːˈeɪɾɪŋ, fɔːɹ ðiːz bᵻlˈɔŋ tə wˈɔnt ænd bˈɑːndɪdʒ.

lines.text: This is the Advaita. Our relation to It is that we are It. Misery is thinking ourselves separate; liberation is knowing our unity.
lines.ph: ðɪs ɪz ðˈə ədvˈaɪtə. ˌaʊɚ ɹᵻlˈeɪʃən tʊ ɪɾ ɪz ðˈæt wiː ɑːɹ ɪt. mˈɪzɚɹi ɪz θˈɪŋkɪŋ aʊɚsˈɛlvz sˈɛpɹət; lˌɪbɚɹˈeɪʃən ɪz nˈoʊɪŋ ˌaʊɚ jˈuːnɪɾi.

lines.text: Only here is there a reason for ethics: the universe is one, so in hurting anyone I hurt myself, and in loving anyone I love myself.
lines.ph: ˈoʊnli hˈɪɹ ɪz ðɛɹ ɐ ɹˈiːzən fɔːɹ ˈɛθɪks: ðə jˈuːnɪvˌɜːs ɪz wˌʌn, sˌoʊ ɪn hˈɜːɾɪŋ ˈɛnɪwˌʌn aɪ hˈɜːt maɪsˈɛlf, ænd ɪn lˈʌvɪŋ ˈɛnɪwˌʌn aɪ lˈʌv maɪsˈɛlf.

lines.text: What India needs now, he says, is not so much weeping, but a little strength.
lines.ph: wˌʌt ˈɪndiə nˈiːdz nˈaʊ, hiː sˈɛz, ɪz nˌɑːt sˈoʊ mˌʌtʃ wˈiːpɪŋ, bˌʌt ɐ lˈɪɾəl stɹˈɛŋθ.

lines.text: Man stands on the glory of his own soul, which no weapon can pierce, no fire burn, no water melt, no air dry.
lines.ph: mˈæn stˈændz ɔnðə ɡlˈoːɹi ʌv hɪz ˈoʊn sˈoʊl, wˌɪtʃ nˈoʊ wˈɛpən kæn pˈɪɹs, nˈoʊ fˈaɪɚ bˈɜːn, nˈoʊ wˈɔːɾɚ mˈɛlt, nˈoʊ ˈɛɹ dɹˈaɪ.

lines.text: Before its magnitude, the suns and moons and all their systems are drops in the ocean.
lines.ph: bᵻfˌoːɹ ɪts mˈæɡnɪtˌuːd, ðə sˈʌnz ænd mˈuːnz ænd ˈɔːl ðɛɹ sˈɪstəmz ɑːɹ dɹˈɑːps ɪnðɪ ˈoʊʃən.

lines.text: Whatever you think, that you will be.
lines.ph: wʌtˈɛvɚ juː θˈɪŋk, ðæt juː wɪl bˈiː.

lines.text: Think yourselves weak, and weak you will be. Think yourselves strong, and strong you will be.
lines.ph: θˈɪŋk joːɹsˈɛlvz wˈiːk, ænd wˈiːk juː wɪl bˈiː. θˈɪŋk joːɹsˈɛlvz stɹˈɔŋ, ænd stɹˈɔŋ juː wɪl bˈiː.

lines.text: Make your children strong from childhood. Let them learn, first of all, the glory of the soul.
lines.ph: mˌeɪk jʊɹ tʃˈɪldɹən stɹˈɔŋ fɹʌm tʃˈaɪldhʊd. lˈɛt ðˌɛm lˈɜːn, fˈɜːst ʌv ˈɔːl, ðə ɡlˈoːɹi ʌvðə sˈoʊl.

lines.text: India has many sects, and the mystery is that they do not quarrel.
lines.ph: ˈɪndiə hɐz mˈɛni sˈɛkts, ænd ðə mˈɪstɚɹi ɪz ðæt ðeɪ duːnˌɑːt kwˈɔːɹəl.

lines.text: The Shaivite does not say the Vaishnavite will be damned. This is my path, and you have yours; at the end we come together.
lines.ph: ðˈə ʃˈaɪvaɪt dʌznˌɑːt sˈeɪ ðə vˈaɪʃnəvaɪt wɪl biː dˈæmd. ðɪs ɪz maɪ pˈæθ, ænd juː hæv jˈoːɹz; æt ðɪ ˈɛnd wiː kˈʌm təɡˈɛðɚ.

lines.text: Each has an Ishta, a chosen path, because different natures need different methods.
lines.ph: ˈiːtʃ hɐz æn ˈɪʃtə, ɐ tʃˈoʊzən pˈæθ, bɪkˈʌz dˈɪfɹənt nˈeɪtʃɚz nˈiːd dˈɪfɹənt mˈɛθədz.

lines.text: Woe unto the world when everyone is of the same religious opinion and takes to the same path.
lines.ph: wˈoʊ ˌʌntʊ ðə wˈɜːld wɛn ˈɛvɹɪwˌʌn ɪz ʌvðə sˈeɪm ɹᵻlˈɪdʒəs əpˈɪniən ænd tˈeɪks tə ðə sˈeɪm pˈæθ.

lines.text: Variety is the very soul of life.
lines.ph: vɚɹˈaɪəɾi ɪz ðə vˈɛɹi sˈoʊl ʌv lˈaɪf.

lines.text: If a temple, a symbol or an image helps you, have two hundred images if you like. But the moment you quarrel, you are going backward, towards the brutes.
lines.ph: ɪf ɐ tˈɛmpəl, ɐ sˈɪmbəl ɔːɹ ɐn ˈɪmɪdʒ hˈɛlps juː, hæv tˈuː hˈʌndɹɪd ˈɪmɪdʒᵻz ɪf juː lˈaɪk. bˌʌt ðə mˈoʊmənt juː kwˈɔːɹəl, juː ɑːɹ ɡˌoʊɪŋ bˈækwɚd, təwˈɔːɹdz ðə bɹˈuːts.

lines.text: Caste and other institutions are not the religion. They protect the nation, and will die a natural death when they are no longer needed.
lines.ph: kˈæst ænd ˈʌðɚɹ ˌɪnstɪtˈuːʃənz ɑːɹ nˌɑːt ðə ɹᵻlˈɪdʒən. ðeɪ pɹətˈɛkt ðə nˈeɪʃən, ænd wɪl dˈaɪ ɐ nˈætʃɚɹəl dˈɛθ wɛn ðeɪ ɑːɹ nˌoʊ lˈɑːŋɡɚ nˈiːdᵻd.

lines.text: Yet the older he grows, the less he wants to curse any of them, for each embodies the experience of centuries.
lines.ph: jˈɛt ðɪ ˈoʊldɚ hiː ɡɹˈoʊz, ðə lˈɛs hiː wˈɔnts tə kˈɜːs ˌɛni ʌv ðˌɛm, fɔːɹ ˈiːtʃ ɛmbˈɑːdiz ðɪ ɛkspˈiəɹɪəns ʌv sˈɛntʃɚɹiz.

lines.text: Much advice from abroad is like that of a child of yesterday, destined to die the day after tomorrow.
lines.ph: mˈʌtʃ ɐdvˈaɪs fɹʌm ɐbɹˈɔːd ɪz lˈaɪk ðæt əvə tʃˈaɪld ʌv jˈɛstɚdˌeɪ, dˈɛstɪnd tə dˈaɪ ðə dˈeɪ ˈæftɚ təmˈɑːɹoʊ.

lines.text: Born like moths in the spring and dying in five minutes; coming up like bubbles, and bursting like bubbles too.
lines.ph: bˈɔːɹn lˈaɪk mˈɑːθs ɪnðə spɹˈɪŋ ænd dˈaɪɪŋ ɪn fˈaɪv mˈɪnɪts; kˈʌmɪŋ ˌʌp lˈaɪk bˈʌbəlz, ænd bˈɜːstɪŋ lˈaɪk bˈʌbəlz tˈuː.

lines.text: First make a society that stands through scores of centuries.
lines.ph: fˈɜːst mˌeɪk ɐ səsˈaɪəɾi ðæt stˈændz θɹuː skˈoːɹz ʌv sˈɛntʃɚɹiz.

lines.text: Till then, my friend, you are only a giddy child.
lines.ph: tˈɪl ðˈɛn, maɪ fɹˈɛnd, juː ɑːɹ ˈoʊnli ɐ ɡˈɪdi tʃˈaɪld.

lines.text: One pressing need remains. Praise be to Vyasa, the author of the Mahabharata: in this Kali Yuga there is one great work.
lines.ph: wˈʌn pɹˈɛsɪŋ nˈiːd ɹᵻmˈeɪnz. pɹˈeɪz biː tuː vjˈɑːsə, ðɪ ˈɔːθɚɹ ʌvðə məhˌɑːbˈɑːɹətə: ɪn ðˈɪs kˈʌli jˈʊɡə ðɛɹ ɪz wˈʌn ɡɹˈeɪt wˈɜːk.

lines.text: The hard austerities of other ages do not work now. What is needed is Dana: giving, helping others.
lines.ph: ðə hˈɑːɹd ɔːstˈɛɹᵻɾiz ʌv ˈʌðɚɹ ˈeɪdʒᵻz duːnˌɑːt wˈɜːk nˈaʊ. wˌʌt ɪz nˈiːdᵻd ɪz dˈɑːnə: ɡˈɪvɪŋ, hˈɛlpɪŋ ˈʌðɚz.

lines.text: The highest gift is spiritual knowledge; next, secular knowledge; then the saving of life; and last, food and drink.
lines.ph: ðə hˈaɪɪst ɡˈɪft ɪz spˈɪɹɪtʃˌuːəl nˈɑːlɪdʒ; nˈɛkst, sˈɛkjʊlɚ nˈɑːlɪdʒ; ðˈɛn ðə sˈeɪvɪŋ ʌv lˈaɪf; ænd lˈæst, fˈuːd ænd dɹˈɪŋk.

lines.text: Talking is not religion. Parrots may talk; machines may talk nowadays.
lines.ph: tˈɔːkɪŋ ɪz nˌɑːt ɹᵻlˈɪdʒən. pˈæɹəts mˈeɪ tˈɔːk; məʃˈiːnz mˈeɪ tˈɔːk nˈaʊədˌeɪz.

lines.text: Bring the treasures out of the closed books, and deliver them to their rightful heirs, rich and poor, in India and all over the world.
lines.ph: bɹˈɪŋ ðə tɹˈɛʒɚz ˌaʊɾəv ðə klˈoʊzd bˈʊks, ænd dᵻlˈɪvɚ ðˌɛm tə ðɛɹ ɹˈaɪtfəl ˈɛɹz, ɹˈɪtʃ ænd pˈʊɹ, ɪn ˈɪndiə ænd ˈɔːl ˌoʊvɚ ðə wˈɜːld.

lines.text: The more you help others, the more you help yourselves.
lines.ph: ðə mˈoːɹ juː hˈɛlp ˈʌðɚz, ðə mˈoːɹ juː hˈɛlp joːɹsˈɛlvz.

lines.text: Above all, for ages there has been jealousy, even a wish for precedence in the worship of God.
lines.ph: əbˌʌv ˈɔːl, fɔːɹ ˈeɪdʒᵻz ðɛɹ hˈæzbiːn dʒˈɛləsi, ˈiːvən ɐ wˈɪʃ fɔːɹ pɹˈɛsᵻdəns ɪnðə wˈɜːʃɪp ʌv ɡˈɑːd.

lines.text: Everyone wants to command, and no one wants to obey.
lines.ph: ˈɛvɹɪwˌʌn wˈɔnts tə kəmˈænd, ænd nˈoʊwˈʌn wˈɔnts tʊ oʊbˈeɪ.

lines.text: First, learn to obey. The command will come by itself.
lines.ph: fˈɜːst, lˈɜːn tʊ oʊbˈeɪ. ðə kəmˈænd wɪl kˈʌm baɪ ɪtsˈɛlf.

lines.text: Learn first to be a servant, and you will be fit to be a master.
lines.ph: lˈɜːn fˈɜːst təbi ɐ sˈɜːvənt, ænd juː wɪl biː fˈɪt təbi ɐ mˈæstɚ.

lines.text: Our ancestors did wonderful works. We too will do great deeds, so that others look back on us with blessings and pride.
lines.ph: ˌaʊɚɹ ˈænsɛstɚz dˈɪd wˈʌndɚfəl wˈɜːks. wiː tˈuː wɪl dˈuː ɡɹˈeɪt dˈiːdz, sˌoʊ ðæt ˈʌðɚz lˈʊk bˈæk ˌɔn ˌʌs wɪð blˈɛsɪŋz ænd pɹˈaɪd.

lines.text: From Jaffna, the Swami crosses the strait to India, to Pamban.
lines.ph: fɹˈʌm dʒˈɑːfnə, ðˈə swˈɑːmi kɹˈɔsᵻz ðə stɹˈeɪt tʊ ˈɪndiə, tˈuː pˈɑːmbən.
